newsitem.title: INDIA: India direct rule in Uttar Pradesh state approved.
newsitem.headline: India direct rule in Uttar Pradesh state approved.

text.p: The Indian parliament on Thursday approved a second consecutive extension of New Delhi's direct rule in the most populous state of Uttar Pradesh following inconclusive elections there in October.
The Lok Sabha, or lower hosue of parliament, voted for the extension by voice vote. Deputies from the main opposition Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) walked out.

Home Minister Inderjit Gupta told the Lok Sabha that the hung state assembly indicated a severe polarisation of parties along the Hindu caste system, saying it was a threat to the country's 50-year old democratic rule.

"The way the factor of casteism has dominated the thinking of the people and the polarisation of parties, I am afraid it is going to spell the death knell of democracy in the country," Gupta said. "All parties have been tainted in this respect."
The BJP, regarded by its opponents as an upper caste Hindu party, fell short of a majority in the Uttar Pradesh polls but had claimed it could win a majority if alllowed to form a government.
The move was opposed by the socialist Samajwadi Party, a key partner in Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's United Front alliance, which has it support base among the middle caste farmers.
Both tried unsuccessfully to woo the Bahujan Samaj Party of the lowest caste Hindu groups to form a government.
